evidence.observation: "`run()` bounds each file it will retain (each payload holds at most its" / "stage's scheduled sections times the response cap) and refuses if a bound" / "exceeds the retained-file cap." Nothing limits this rule to caller roots or live producers.

"response (128 KiB, today's effective bound, since a response cannot exceed the 128 KiB read of `responses.json`; ceiling 1 MiB)" and "retained file (128 KiB, today's read of a run's own files; ceiling 64 MiB)". Under both defaults, a single scheduled section already bounds a payload at 128 KiB plus its attempt metadata, which reading.py:188-193 adds to every attempt: section, source, start, end, source_version and two sha256 values. That exceeds the 128 KiB retained-file cap, and two sections bound the payload at 256 KiB.

evidence.location: §4 LH1-C1 and LH1-C9, line 370; §0 R0.2, lines 85-88
evidence.observation: LH1-C1 reads "a test producer with no `calls` attribute drives six stages over the caller root (two sources, its own model and include" and names no limits; LH2-C3 treats non-default limits as a separate case. LH1-C9 reads "the three packaged run configurations equal the trees recorded at `4ad0d216`". The packaged reading_fixture/roster.json schedules three opening sections (study-opening, annex-opening, control-table) and three targeted ones. Under R0.4's one loop, payload-1's bound is therefore 3 x 128 KiB, so the packaged run would refuse before its first call and write no /1 bytes.

concerns.recommendation: Reconcile the defaults with the bound rule. Either derive the default retained-file cap of a /2 run from the other limits (scheduled sections x response cap plus per-attempt overhead), or bound SavedProducer runs by the known sizes of their saved responses and apply the refusal to live /2 runs only. State the overhead term, and name the limits LH1-C1 runs with.
concerns.title: Fixes 3 and 5 together: under D4's defaults the retained-file bound refuses every live run, and the packaged run, before the first call

evidence.observation: "a run at the response and roster ceilings, with the retained-file cap raised to fit, completes"

D4 sets "roster cap (default 128, ceiling 4,096)", a response ceiling of 1 MiB and "retained file (128 KiB, today's read of a run's own files; ceiling 64 MiB)". At the roster ceiling a stage can schedule 4,096 sections. The plan's own rule, "each payload holds at most its stage's scheduled sections times the response cap", then gives a bound of 4,096 x 1 MiB = 4 GiB, and the captured response table holds every stage's responses. Because the retained-file cap stops at 64 MiB, at the response ceiling no stage with more than about 63 scheduled sections can run. A roster at the ceiling with almost every section unscheduled is the only way to meet the criterion.
"including the LH1-C14 run at the response and roster ceilings `(p1)`" rests on the same run.

concerns.recommendation: Either raise the retained-file ceiling to cover the roster ceiling x the response ceiling and hold it to R0.8's time bound, or restate LH1-C14 as a run whose computed bound equals the retained-file ceiling. Say in D4 that the ceilings cannot all be reached together, and give the number of sections that run schedules.
concerns.title: LH1-C14's completing run at the response and roster ceilings exceeds the retained-file ceiling

evidence.observation: "A fact type is attached when one of its roles is played by the assertion entity." and "The packaged model's `assertion` is such an entity, so the packaged example stays on the packaged path."

"requirements, each with an ID, an attached fact type, a role, the" ... "A requirement naming an unknown fact type or role refuses the call." ... "A call with rules and no shape is a packaged-shape `/2` call". In the packaged model, polarity and attribution are roles of the objectified `assertion_statement` (assertion_admission.py:22, :31-34, :122), and the `assertion` entity plays no role in it. The plan therefore never says which fact types a caller's rule may name on the packaged shape, or which fact type the default rules name.

concerns.recommendation: State that on the packaged shape the one fact type a requirement may name is `assertion_statement`, with one row per assertion. Name that fact type in the default rules, and say whether a rule naming `assertion_names_work` or `assertion_names_passage` refuses there.

evidence.observation: "The packaged projection keeps `MAX_TARGETS` as" / "its row bound (`:46`), so its bytes do not move."

"A call with any new argument (a shape, rules, `max_targets` or" / "`max_rows`) writes `literature-assertion-admission/2`" and a /2 record "records `max_targets` and `max_rows`". A packaged-shape call that passes `max_rows` therefore writes a /2 record carrying a row bound the packaged projection never applies. The plan does not say whether such a call refuses or treats `max_rows` as inert, and LH4-C7 does not cover the case.

concerns.recommendation: Either refuse `max_rows` when no shape is given, or record it as not applicable on the packaged shape, and add the case to LH4-C7.
